entities.text:
HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  Criminal Revision No.507/2020  (Mustafa Vs. State of M.P.)
Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Ravindra Upadhyay, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Sandeep Mehta, learned counsel for the respondent.
Heard on IA No. 854/2020, which is first application under Section 397(1) of the Code of Procedure for suspension of jail sentence and for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant- Mustafa.

The applicant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 16(I) A(I) 16 (II) of Prevention of Food adulteration Act and sentenced to undergo 3 years R.I. each and fine of Rs.
10,000/-, Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jobat, District Alirajpur vide judgment dated 08.10.2015 passed in Criminal Case No.670/2011.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Jobat, District Alirajpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, the appliant has preferred Criminal Appeal before the Sessions Court which was partly allowed and sentence imposed upon the applicant was reduced from 3 years R.I. to 6 months R.I.
however, fine amount has been enhanced from Rs.10,000/- to Rs. 15,000/-.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant was on bail during the trial as well as appeal and he did not misuse the liberty so granted to him.
It is further submitted that the offence alleged to have been registered on 22.01.2011 at about 01:00 pm and after completion of the enquiry, complaint was filed on 14.07.2011.

Meanwhile Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was repealed and act was placed in Second Schedule of Food Safety Act, 2006 and Section 97 of the Act provides that with effect from such date, as the Central Government may appoint in this behalf the enactment of the order specified in the Second Schedule shall stand repealed.

The Government issued a notification F.No.P-15025/41/2011- DQFC, dated 4th August, 2011 according to which so far as Chapter 9 is concerned, section 48 to 80 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 were notified and enforced by S.O.1855(E), dated 29 th July, 2010.
In the present case charges were framed on 19.04.2014 under the P.F.A. Act 1954 which was repealed way back in the year 2011.
Therefore, the trial court as well as appellate have committed error in convicting the applicant for the said offence.
Under these circumstances, he prays for suspension of custodial sentence of the applicant.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and short sentence is involved in the matter and the fact that petition is likely to take time for final hearing, IA No. 854/2020 is allowed and the jail sentence alone passed against the applicant shall remain suspended and the applicant is directed to be released on bail upon him furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court, for his regular appearance before this Court on 05/05/2019 and on such further dates as may be fixed in behalf by the Registry during pendency of this petition.
